question: Can separate worker directories start no more than one native team for an enrolled ticket, even if a durable admission reply is lost?
population: 18 new native Shift Board scripted tickets; three assigned worker identities. No model or provider key. A spent ticket is not a completed trial.
environment: Independent worker directories and processes on one machine. Same Docker engine. Central coordinator uses a private disk; no shared worker trial directory. No SSH link or remote durability claim.

local_only.method: Two sequential stock run-next commands on disjoint empty roots with one logical owner. Do not overlap two Docker jobs for the same old ticket.
local_only.pass: Two distinct native trial IDs, each with a replayed grade. Joined collection keeps the single ticket ambiguous.

race.method: Two simultaneously started admitted worker processes, same ticket and owner, disjoint roots and nonces.
race.pass: Exactly one grant, one denial, one native ID and independently replayed grade.

lost_reply.method: Persist the grant, discard the whole reply before worker sees it. Restart serve-once on the same ledger; ask from a fresh root.
lost_reply.pass: Neither worker has a native start, second request is denied, ticket stays issued and its grade stays unknown.

unrelated.method: Use the assigned different worker after the lost reply.
unrelated.pass: One new grant and one independently replayed native grade.

primary_pass: All 4 units pass on first attempts. Across the 18 tickets the admitted cohort has 3 issued, 2 unique native grades and 16 unknown. The two local-only starts form a separate comparison and never fill an admitted slot. No automatic retry.
out_of_scope: Safety if the ledger is copied, rolled back or bypassed
Crash survival without a durable local filesystem and trusted coordinator
